answer: Sybil resistance follows from an exponential temporal half-life: an identity must deliver sustained honest service or its reputation rapidly decays. The EigenTrust kernel combines normalized endorsements, reciprocity weights, and transitive support, while temporal scoring limits old evidence. A freshly spawned Sybil has near-zero eigenvector centrality and no established trusted paths, so it cannot pass consensus; multiplying accounts only spreads negligible pigment across the trust terrace rather than creating influence.
